newsitem.title: USA: DC's sale of $274 mln in notes "positive"-official.
newsitem.headline: DC's sale of $274 mln in notes "positive"-official.

text.p: The District of Columbia's sale Wednesday of $274 million in short-term notes was "very positive," Thomas Huestis, deputy finance chief for the city, told Reuters.
Huestis said $200 million in tax revenue anticipation notes maturing Sept. 30, 1997, sold at a 4.50 coupon price to yield 3.98.
Another $74 million in budget notes maturing Sept. 30, 1998, sold at 3.98 at par, Huestis said.
Lehman Brothers Inc. and Morgan Stanley & Co. were underwriters on both negotiated deals, with Lehman serving as book manager.
"We had over 20 institutions offering bids on the TRANS," Huestis said. "That compares to three (bids) a year ago. And we had another 112-15 institutions on the GO notes."

"My overall reaction is very positive," Huestis said. "The additional institutional investors that participated and put in bids demonstrated that the District continues to improve its financial health. Even though we didn't have a great market today, we still got these done at a very competitive rate," Huestis added.
Huestis said the city had over $300 million in orders for the TRANS and $150 million in orders for the budget notes.
